<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Systemic vascular dysfunction has been implicated in parkinsonism, but prospective evidence on the cumulative burden of multisystem vascular-related disease (MVRD) and its relation to genetic susceptibility remains limited. We included 456,862 UK Biobank participants of White ethnicity with available genetic data who were free of diagnosed parkinsonism at baseline. MVRD comprised ischemic heart disease, stroke, chronic kidney disease, retinopathy, and neuropathy. Incident parkinsonism, excluding vascular parkinsonism, was ascertained during follow-up. Fine–Gray competing-risk models were used to estimate subdistribution hazard ratios (sHRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs), with all-cause mortality treated as the competing event. During a median follow-up of 11.8 years, 2559 incident parkinsonism cases occurred. Any MVRD was associated with a higher risk of parkinsonism (sHR 1.35; 95% CI 1.23, 1.48), and each additional MVRD-related condition was associated with a higher risk (sHR 1.30; 95% CI 1.21, 1.40). The associations increased with the number of MVRD-related conditions, with sHRs of 1.29, 1.73, and 2.52 for one, two, and three or more conditions, respectively, compared with none. The association between MVRD and parkinsonism was observed in both low- and high-genetic-risk groups, with no evidence of interaction. Results remained broadly consistent after excluding cases diagnosed during the first 10 years of follow-up. These findings suggest a graded association between MVRD burden and incident parkinsonism, adding to the evidence linking vascular health to neurodegeneration.</jats:p>
title: Association of multisystem vascular-related disease with incident parkinsonism: insights from a cohort study

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Ordinary Portland cement (OPC) matrices are widely used in low and intermediate level radioactive waste immobilization; however, improvements in waste loading, workability, durability, and radionuclide retention remain desirable. This work investigates the influence of nano-γ-Al₂O₃ modification on the short-and long-term solidification and stabilization performance of OPC-based cesium-bearing waste forms under ideal and realistic curing conditions. The synthesized nano-γ-Al₂O₃ particles exhibited mesoporous morphology, reactive hydroxylated surfaces, and negative surface charge suitable for cementitious applications. Under ideal curing conditions, nano-γ-Al₂O₃ displayed a non-monotonic dosage-dependent effect on the hydration and solidification behavior due to multi-variable interactions leading to changes in the nano- and matrix-chemical conditions thus affecting the pore-solution chemistry, and hydration pathways. 5 wt.% modified matrix provided improved workability, enhanced volumetric stability, and acceptable mechanical performance. Under realistic curing conditions and maximum waste loading, the 5 wt.% nano-γ-Al₂O₃ matrices maintained their favorable processing. Mineralogical, spectroscopic, and microstructural analyses revealed the formation of Al-rich hydration assemblages, including AFt, AFm, and hydroxo-AFm phases and the presence of more hydroxylated species in the modified matrix. Elemental-ratio distributions in pristine and leached matrices indicated that Cesium binding is primarily associated with C-S-H/C-A-S-H and AFt/AFm hydration products. The results demonstrate that while nano-γ-Al₂O₃ effectively tailors the workability and hydration pathways under representative waste-conditioning conditions, its implementation involves a performance trade-off between processing behavior, mechanical integrity, and long-term cesium retention.</jats:p>
title: Elucidating cesium solidification and stabilization mechanisms in nano-gamma-alumina modified cementitious matrices under realistic conditions

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Genetic causes are identified in up to 15% of Parkinson’s disease (PD) patients; the remaining idiopathic PD (iPD) patients are attributed to polygenic risk, environmental and lifestyle factors, and interactions thereof. We applied five advanced polygenic score (PGS) tools to data from 1762 iPD patients and 4227 healthy controls of European ancestry. 5-fold cross-validation revealed a significant boost in the discriminative power of modern Bayesian methods over simpler approaches, leading to the development of a novel iPD-PGS. This score demonstrated significantly improved performance compared to existing scores, achieving an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.680 (95% confidence interval (-CI):[0.665, 0.695]). External validation confirmed its robustness. Early-onset iPD patients exhibited higher PGS values than late-onset iPD patients and healthy controls, indicating increased polygenetic burden. Applying our novel iPD-PGS to carriers of heterozygous
                    <jats:italic>PRKN</jats:italic>
                    variants and
                    <jats:italic>GBA1</jats:italic>
                    coding risk variants suggested that penetrance in these groups is partly explained by the same polygenic alterations as observed mitigating iPD.
                    <jats:italic>GBA1</jats:italic>
                    showed a trend toward higher discriminative potential than
                    <jats:italic>PRKN</jats:italic>
                    (
                    <jats:italic>GBA1</jats:italic>
                    : AUC = 0.639, 95%-CI:[0.590, 0.687];
                    <jats:italic>PRKN</jats:italic>
                    : AUC = 0.594, 95%-CI:[0.501, 0.687]), though confidence intervals overlapped. Our study highlights the potential of advanced PGSs in PD research, particularly in identifying high-risk individuals and modifying risk in rare-variant carriers.
                  </jats:p>
title: A state-of-the-art polygenic score for idiopathic Parkinson’s disease: benchmarking methods and impact on genetic PD carriers

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Electrochemical anodization improves the surface properties of titanium implants, but the resulting oxide layer may be damaged by plastic deformation during insertion or service. This study investigated how four deformation levels, together with an undeformed reference, affect anodized Ti6Al4V ELI. Surface morphology, roughness, wettability, microstructure, cytocompatibility, and electrochemical behavior were evaluated. Deformation progressively increased surface roughness and induced micro- and macrocracking of the anodic layer, while all surfaces remained hydrophilic. Damage to the oxide markedly reduced corrosion protection: the corrosion rate increased from approx. 50 to 650 nm year⁻¹, whereas polarization resistance decreased from 11,920 to 327 kΩ·cm². Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy indicated facilitated ionic transport through deformation-induced defects. Nevertheless, no cytotoxic effect on MC3T3-E1 cells was observed, and differences in cell viability were not statistically significant. Thus, plastic deformation substantially impairs the electrochemical barrier function of anodized Ti6Al4V ELI without adversely affecting its short-term cytocompatibility.</jats:p>
title: Effect of plastic deformation on corrosion, biological and technological properties of anodized Ti6Al4V ELI implants

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Strain engineering has been an effective strategy for enhancing carrier transport in Si-based transistors. However, in atomically thin 2D materials, strain transfer is hindered by a weak van der Waals (vdW) interface, and global or substrate-mediated strain is difficult to apply effectively. Thus, strain engineering produces limited effects on performance improvement. To overcome these challenges, we report a contact-localized strain engineering approach using metal stressors for MoS
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    transistors. Effective strain is induced when three key mechanical conditions are satisfied: (1) metal nanoisland formation at the interface between metal and MoS
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    enabled by intermediate adhesion, moderate surface tension, and high adatom diffusivity on MoS
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    ; (2) strain generation arising from lattice and atomic registry interactions between the metal and MoS
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    at the interface; and (3) strain transfer through a finite vdW gap that suppresses hybridization while allowing shear coupling. The tensile strain in MoS
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    is exclusively confined to the footprint of the metal nanoisland and integrates to an average global strain of ~0.2%, while the interface remains non-reactive. This engineered strain lowers the effective Schottky barrier height by ~50 meV and reduces contact resistance by ~30%, thereby increasing the on-current by ~60% compared with otherwise identical unstrained devices. This work positions contact-localized strain control as a promising design knob for preparing high-performance 2D transistors.
                  </jats:p>
title: Contact-localized, strain-engineered metal contacts in 2D field-effect transistors: enabling low-barrier injection via a local stressor

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Lectin receptors recognize specific glycan features within heterogeneous glycan populations to initiate immune signaling, yet how defined signals are extracted from structurally diverse ligand mixtures remains poorly understood. Here we report the molecular basis by which the innate immune receptor Dectin-1 recognizes the soluble β-glucan laminarin. Native mass spectrometry revealed that laminarin exists as heterogeneous chains spanning a degree of polymerization (DP) of 22–44, while Dectin-1 is strictly monomeric in solution. Isotopic mass tagging with uniformly ¹³C-labeled Dectin-1 established a preferred 3:3 receptor-to-laminarin stoichiometry (~80–85 kDa). Flow-induced dispersion analysis demonstrated cooperative binding with an apparent dissociation constant of 46 μM and a Hill coefficient of ~3, accompanied by a large increase in hydrodynamic radius. Analysis of the bound ligand fraction revealed selective enrichment of chains with DP 25–36, defining a preferred chain-length window. High-speed atomic force microscopy showed that individual Dectin-1 molecules undergo cooperative clustering on both laminarin and the longer β-glucan scleroglucan, while chemical crosslinking provided independent evidence for ligand-induced receptor association. Together, these findings demonstrate that β-glucan recognition by Dectin-1 is governed by chain-length selectivity and cooperative receptor assembly, consistent with a molecular ruler mechanism in which lectin receptors extract specific biological information from heterogeneous glycan populations.</jats:p>
title: Chain-length-selective cooperative assembly underlies β-glucan recognition by Dectin-1

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Parkinson’s disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by dopaminergic neuronal loss, oxidative stress, and debilitating motor dysfunction. Targeting the Wnt signaling pathway provides a powerful disease-modifying strategy. Building on recent evidence that triazine derivatives modulate Wnt signaling, we used a
                    <jats:italic>Drosophila</jats:italic>
                    model and in silico molecular docking to validate the specific interactions driving this pathway modulation, followed by qPCR of key Wnt signaling-related genes:
                    <jats:italic>armadillo</jats:italic>
                    ,
                    <jats:italic>wingless</jats:italic>
                    , and
                    <jats:italic>frizzled 3</jats:italic>
                    . The neuroprotective efficacy of the triazine derivative, alone or in combination with curcumin or resveratrol, was subsequently evaluated using behavioral, neurochemical, biochemical, apoptotic, immunohistochemical, and ultrastructural assessments. Treatment with the triazine derivative produced marked neuroprotective effects, which were further enhanced when combined with curcumin or resveratrol. This treatment significantly restored dopamine levels and locomotor performance, enhanced superoxide dismutase and catalase activities, and reduced lipid peroxidation compared with untreated rotenone-exposed flies. Moreover, immunohistochemical analysis indicated attenuation of apoptotic signaling, while transmission electron microscopy revealed substantial preservation of neural ultrastructure. Collectively, these findings demonstrate the neuroprotective potential of the triazine derivative and suggest that its combination with curcumin and resveratrol may provide an enhanced strategy for counteracting oxidative stress, neural apoptosis, and motor dysfunction associated with PD. The findings further support Wnt signaling modulation as a promising mechanistic target and provide a rationale for further investigations of triazine-based combination strategies as potential disease-modifying approaches for PD.
                  </jats:p>
title: Synergistic interplay between triazine and curcumin or resveratrol in mitigating rotenone-induced toxicity in Drosophila model

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Political regimes lack a stable endpoint: they shift between more and less democratic configurations over time, as illustrated by historical democratic waves and recent backsliding. We analyse the historical trajectories of countries within a two-dimensional regime space derived from the principal components of the Varieties of Democracy dataset. We observe dynamics consistent with weak non-ergodicity, unfolding in an effective landscape of sparse and shifting basins of stability. Step sizes and sojourn times follow heavy-tailed distributions near the critical regime where mean values diverge, pointing to intermittent and heterogeneous regime change. A continuous time random walk model reproduces the average dynamics and trajectory-to-trajectory variability of the last three decades. The temporal evolution of the ergodicity breaking parameter recovers waves of democratisation and periods of heightened global political divergence, demonstrating the framework’s diagnostic potential. These results suggest that political regime evolution follows universal stochastic principles while remaining punctuated by unique historical pathways.</jats:p>
title: Critical dynamics govern the evolution of political regimes

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The phase space (velocity and real space) dynamics of bulk ions is a critical issue for the heating scenario in magnetically confined plasma. Bulk ions accelerate parallel to the magnetic field, and the velocity distribution function can depart from a Maxwellian due to wave-particle interactions such as Landau and transit-time damping. Here we show flattening in velocity space (a decrease in the velocity gradient) and a rapid increase in ion energy parallel to the magnetic field within 0.1 ms of the onset of the MHD burst, by 30% at the location of the MHD burst in the Large Helical Device. In velocity space, the anisotropy of ion-velocity distribution due to the acceleration of ions parallel to the magnetic field disappears within the ion-ion collision time scale (2  ~ 3 ms). The transient increase in ion energy decays within 6 ms at the plasma periphery but persists much longer in the plasma core, contributing to the rise in core-ion energy.</jats:p>
title: Direct observation of phase-space dynamics during energetic-particle-driven MHD bursts

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Membrane transport is a fundamental biological process with profound implications for pharmacology, biotechnology, and microbiology. While computational approaches have largely adopted a protein-centric perspective to annotate transportomes, inferring transport function directly from the intrinsic properties of substrates remains a major challenge. Addressing transport at the compound level enables the systematic evaluation of whether molecules undergo active transport and by which mechanisms, independent of prior transporter annotation. Here, we introduce ChemProFlow, a comprehensive computational framework that redefines transport analysis from a substrate-centric perspective. By integrating geometric deep learning with orthology-based genomic mapping, ChemProFlow predicts molecular transportability, assigns transport mechanisms according to the Transporter Classification Database, and identifies the microorganisms encoding the corresponding transport systems. We show that this integrated pipeline enables scalable, end-to-end mapping of substrate-transporter-organism relationships, with broad applications in pharmacology for anticipating drug transport, in biotechnology for guiding strain engineering, and in microbiology for dissecting substrate utilization across diverse taxa. By capturing the chemical determinants of transportability, ChemProFlow generalizes to previously unseen substrates and provides a high-throughput framework for systematic exploration of molecular transport across diverse biological contexts.</jats:p>
title: End-to-end mapping of membrane transport from chemical structure to microorganisms

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Asymmetric arm swing reduction is a hallmark of early-stage Parkinson’s disease (PD). We evaluated wrist sensor-based arm swing measures during free-living gait as digital progression biomarkers in 623 early-stage PD participants and 50 controls monitored continuously for one year (controls) or two years (PD). Biweekly measures were extracted from detected gait segments without other arm activities using a previously validated signal processing pipeline. Arm swing measures were reduced in PD, reduced on the most affected side, moderately correlated with clinical motor severity, and highly reliable. In unmedicated participants, most affected side measures declined over one year (standardized response means:  −0.34 to  −0.85) and all but one over two years ( −0.57 to  −1.06). The corresponding MDS-UPDRS Part III subscore showed SRMs of  −0.26 (95% CI [−0.66, 0.06]) at one year and  −0.85 (95% CI [-1.95, -0.24]) at two years. In medicated participants, arm swing increased on the most affected side, which was associated with higher dopaminergic doses and dyskinesia. Overall, free-living arm swing measures are promising progression biomarkers in early, untreated PD.</jats:p>
title: Longitudinal progression of digital arm swing measures during free-living gait in early Parkinson’s disease

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Continuous, treatment-responsive measurement of motor state is an unmet need in Parkinson’s disease and a broad challenge for digital biomarkers: clinical gait scales are coarse and ordinal, and most digital measures are never validated beyond their derivation setting. We present a digital biomarker derived from full-mesh 3D human-pose reconstruction in standard monocular video, built from high-contrast within-patient treatment transitions and applied to out-of-sample patients. In a retrospective cohort (53 patients) it discriminated treatment states (cross-validated AUROC 0.88) and defined a continuous motor-state axis. Across six independent cohorts (266 subjects, 3,591 walks, eight sites, three continents) it showed consistent medication effects in the two medication-labelled cohorts and tracked clinical gait impairment in the four cohorts carrying clinical gait ratings; in a prospective cohort (21 patients) it preserved ordered transitions for medication and deep brain stimulation. On identical paired observations it was more responsive than the ordinal MDS-UPDRS Part III item 3.10 (standardized response mean 1.29 versus 0.83 internally, 0.92 versus 0.54 externally); its finer resolution also registered directional within-patient improvement more often, an advantage of measurement resolution that reaches parity once change is required to exceed the minimal detectable change, supporting a scalable, generalizable measurement tool.</jats:p>
title: Computer vision-derived gait-state tracking of acute treatment response in Parkinson’s disease: external and prospective validation
